title: Predicting DRAM-Caused Risky VMs in Large-Scale Clouds
problem: DRAM failures in large-scale clouds are currently mitigated at node granularity, requiring migration of all VMs on a node even when errors affect only a small fraction of the memory address space. This coarse-grained approach consumes excessive resources and causes unnecessary VM disruptions.
motivation: At cloud scale (300,000+ nodes), fine-grained DRAM failure prediction at the VM level can dramatically reduce migration costs and VM crash rates compared to node-level approaches, as DRAM errors are spatially clustered in memory.
method: Pegasus maps DRAM errors (detected using ECC memory error-checking) to specific virtual machines by tracking which memory addresses belong to which VM. A predictor analyzes error-correction patterns and spatial-temporal error clusters (where and when errors happen together) to identify which VMs have memory in at-risk DRAM regions. Rather than migrating all VMs on a server when errors occur, it selectively migrates only the at-risk VMs to healthy hardware.
key_novelty: Pegasus is the first system to predict which individual virtual machines will be affected by DRAM failures by mapping memory errors directly to VMs, enabling selective migration of just the at-risk VMs instead of evacuating entire servers.
contributions: Novel concept of DRAM-caused risky VMs as prediction target for cloud reliability
Error-VM mapping framework correlating physical DRAM error addresses to VM address spaces
Predictor combining ECC and spatio-temporal features achieving prediction performance comparable to node-level approaches
Deployed at production scale on 300,000+ nodes: >70% cost reduction and >10% fewer VM crashes vs. node-level mitigation

metrics.other: >70% lower migration cost vs. node-level; >10% fewer VM crashes; deployed on 300,000+ production nodes

limitations: Not discussed; prediction accuracy figures for specific recall/precision tradeoffs are not provided in the abstract.
primary_theme: VM-granularity DRAM failure prediction for cloud reliability
